caption: PyFDS opens maximized with an empty project: menus and toolbars at the top, the Project Explorer and Properties on the left, the 3D view in the centre.
File menu: New, Open, Save, Import and Export.
File > Project Settings: CHID (the name of every output file) and the case title.

detail.title: Example 1: room fire with door, window, heat detector

caption: Model > Simulation Parameters, Time tab: the simulation ends at T_END = 60 s.
Model > Simulation Parameters: Output tab
Model > Simulation Parameters: Environment tab
Model > Simulation Parameters: Pressure tab
Model > Simulation Parameters: Radiation tab
Model > Add Mesh: a 6 x 4.5 x 3 m domain in 60 x 45 x 30 cells (0.1 m cells, 81,000 in all). 0.1 m is the coarsest cell that resolves this 180 kW fire (validation: D*/dx at least 4).
The mesh appears in the 3D view and under Meshes in the Project Explorer.
Model > Library: the 25 mm gypsum wall construction (two 12.5 mm boards) is added to the project.
Draw > Draw Room: walls, ceiling and two openings - a 0.9 x 2.1 m door in the south wall and a 1.2 x 1.05 m window (sill 0.9 m) in the east wall.
The room (4.8 x 3.3 x 2.4 m inside the mesh) with its door and window.
Model > Add Typed Surface, burner: 500 kW/m2, reached along a t-squared curve in 15 s (TAU_Q = -15).
Model > Add Obstruction: the burner body, a 0.6 x 0.6 x 0.15 m inert block in the middle of the room.

Model > Add Vent: the burning surface is a vent on the top face of the block only (0.36 m2 x 500 kW/m2 = 180 kW). Giving the whole block the burner surface would also burn its four sides and double the fire.
Model > Add Reaction: propane, heat of combustion 46,000 kJ/kg.
Model > Edit Reactions: soot yield 0.024 kg/kg and CO yield 0.005 kg/kg for propane (well-ventilated values, SFPE Handbook, Tewarson). With the default yield of 0 the fire would make no smoke.
Open Mesh Boundaries opens all six faces of the mesh. The floor of a room standing on the ground must stay closed: select DOMAIN_ZMIN_OPEN in the Project Explorer and press Delete.
Model > Library: a heat detector property (RTI 5, activation 74 C).
Model > Add Device: the heat detector 5 cm below the ceiling above the burner.
Model > Add Thermocouple: a vertical tree of four thermocouples at 0.6, 1.2, 1.8 and 2.3 m above the burner centre (the same dialog is used four times).
Model > Add Slice: a temperature slice through the burner (Y = 2.4 m).
Model > Add Slice: a second temperature slice across the room (X = 3.0 m).
Model > Add Slice: a visibility slice at head height (Z = 1.5 m).
The complete model (open-boundary vents hidden): room, door, window, burner, detector and thermocouple tree, and the three slice planes.
Front view (View > Front): the door in the south wall and the burner behind it.
Model > Edit Surfaces: every object of the kind in one list, its settings on the right and the FDS text it will write at the bottom.
Model > Edit Devices: every object of the kind in one list, its settings on the right and the FDS text it will write at the bottom.
Model > Validate: the findings appear in the Validation tab at the bottom. Double-click a finding to select the object it is about.

warnings: Mesh 'DOMAIN': D*/dx ≈ 4.8 — borderline resolution. Recommended ratio is ≥ 10.0.

caption: Run > Run Simulation: where to run (this computer, one process - the model has one mesh), the folder for the input and results, the FDS version, and the 'Before you run' summary of the model and its checks.
Run Monitor at 25 %: progress, heat release rate curve and the last lines of the FDS log.
Run Monitor at 60 %: progress, heat release rate curve and the last lines of the FDS log.
Run Monitor at 90 %: progress, heat release rate curve and the last lines of the FDS log.
Message: Simulation complete
Run finished: 'STOP: FDS completed successfully' in the log, Open Results Viewer enabled.
PyFDS Results (Results > Open PyFDS Results in the editor, or the PyFDS Results shortcut) before a run is loaded.
PyFDS Results, File menu: Load Results opens the .smv file of a run.
File > Load Results with example_1.smv: the geometry is shown and the Navigation View on the left lists every result of the run.
